note:
Batch 1 of 2 for the /pages/ingredients header, modelled on the banner currently there (skingenetix-ingredients-page-banner.jpg) but with our own products.

WHAT THE REFERENCE DOES worth keeping: a row of dropper bottles read left to right, each a visibly DIFFERENT colour, with a bead of serum on the surface. It says 'several distinct actives' in one glance, which is the job of an ingredients-page header. What is not worth keeping: flat diffuse light, unbranded stock bottles, and no reserved type zone. This batch runs the line-up on the brand's primary world - Graphite 1A1A1A, one hard key, real shadows.

PRODUCTS: Copper Peptide (deep blue glass), PDRN Skin Repair (rose-pink) and Glutathione (frosted white). Chosen because their glass colours actually differ - the page's other two serums, Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 and Matrixyl, are both neutral white, so a line-up built from those loses the colour contrast that makes the reference work at a glance.

ALL THREE LABELS ARE QUOTED VERBATIM, and this is the correction that matters. The first cut tried to specify only the front bottle and asked for the other two to be turned away with no legible lettering. The engines rendered full labels on all three anyway and invented what they had not been given: the rose-pink bottle came back reading PORN SKIN REPAIR, twice, at full resolution. An unspecified label in a Class A frame is not an absent label, it is an invented one. PDRN is additionally spelled out letter by letter, which is this project's established fix for that word.

NEGATIVE NOTE: the misread word is deliberately NOT named in the negative list. Luma has no negative-prompt field, so negatives are folded into the prompt body - naming it there would put the word into the prompt and risks both priming it and tripping the content filter. The positive letter-by-letter spelling is the fix.

defaults.negative_global: invented brand name, different brand, altered label, extra text on any product, mangled lettering, gibberish text, registered or trademark symbol, colour names printed as words, four or more bottles, packaging box, carton, botanicals, leaves, flowers, citrus, fruit, wood, stone, linen, scattered pebbles, bokeh sparkle, lens flare, watermark, signature, border, collage, multi-panel layout, clutter, person, hands, face

slots.title: ingredients graphite — A · row of three, type zone left
slots.prompt:
Fine-art product photograph of exactly three 30ml glass dropper serum bottles standing upright in a shallow arc on a seamless deep graphite sweep, colour hex 1A1A1A, falling to near black at the frame edges. The three stand together in the right half of the frame, between 52 and 92 percent of frame width, with clear space around them.

All three share the same bottle form: straight-sided with square shoulders, a brushed satin NEUTRAL SILVER-GREY aluminium collar with a fine vertical brushed grain, and a white rubber-bulb pipette whose bulb is an elongated capsule about 1.6 times taller than wide. Never rose-gold, copper, champagne or chrome-mirror collars.

EVERY BOTTLE'S LABEL IS SPECIFIED AND MUST BE REPRODUCED EXACTLY AS GIVEN - reproduce the front labels as in the attached references, every character verbatim. COLOUR WORDS BELOW DESCRIBE THE INK a line is printed in and must NEVER themselves appear as text on any bottle. No trademark, registered or copyright symbol anywhere.

CENTRE, closest to camera, square to the lens and the sharpest thing in the picture: frosted DEEP BLUE glass, rich at the top fading to pale frosted at the base - keep it BLUE, never navy-black, teal or purple. Its label carries these lines and ONLY these, in order: the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark with the wordmark 'Skingenetix', capital S then lower case; 'COPPER PEPTIDE' in bold capitals on one line; 'ADVANCED' then 'REPAIR SERUM' on two lines; 'PREMIUM FORMULA'; '2% GHK-CU  |  30ML' in small capitals. A narrow vertical rule sits to the left of the text block.

LEFT, slightly behind: frosted ROSE-PINK glass. Its label carries these lines and ONLY these, in order: the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark with the wordmark 'Skingenetix'; the word 'PDRN' - spelled with the four capital letters P, D, R, N - then 'SKIN REPAIR' beneath it, both in bold capitals; 'DEEP RENEWAL' then 'TREATMENT' on two lines; 'PREMIUM FORMULA'; '1% (10,000 PPM) PDRN  |  30ML' in small capitals, again spelling PDRN as P, D, R, N. A narrow vertical rule sits to the left of the text block.

RIGHT, slightly behind: frosted neutral WHITE glass. Its label carries these lines and ONLY these, in order: the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark and the wordmark 'Skingenetix' printed in black ink; 'GLUTATHIONE BRIGHTENING' in black bold capitals on two lines; 'RADIANT GLOW SERUM' in gold bold capitals on two lines; 'PREMIUM FORMULA' in light black capitals; '2% GLUTATHIONE  |  30ML' in small black capitals. A narrow vertical gold rule sits to the left of the text block.

One hard key light from the upper left puts a long specular down each bottle and lays three hard-edged shadows to the right across the sweep; one soft fill. A single clean bead of clear serum rests on the surface in front of the group, catching one highlight. The left 42 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 42 percent of frame width, is empty ground held at even tone and low detail so a headline can sit on it unaided. Shot on a 100mm at f/8, clinical, no styling props.
slots.negative_extra: droppers lying down, spilled liquid, pools of colour, mirror tabletop, bottles touching, second row
